## Why Naming Strategy Matters

Without consistency, the same action fragments across multiple names (`user_searched_something`, `Search Executed`, `search-performed`), breaking queryability and making historical data unusable. A naming strategy prevents this cost entirely.

## Event Names

Pick one format and stick to it across your entire codebase.

### Core Principles

1. **Descriptive** — Use names that clearly describe the action (`Report Created`, not `Action 123`).
2. **Consistent** — One convention across all code, all events.
3. **Contextual** — Keep event names concise; use properties to add detail. `Purchase Completed` with `{ product: 'T-shirt', discount: '20%' }`, not `PurchasedTShirtOnSale`.
4. **Object first** — Name the thing that was acted upon so related events cluster when sorted.
5. **Past tense** — Events are facts about things that already happened.
6. **Describe outcomes, not mechanisms** — Track what the user accomplished (`Report Created`), not how (`Create Button Clicked`). UI coupling breaks on redesigns.

### Option A: `Object Verb` (Title Case)

```
Todo Created
User Invited
Search Performed
Integration Connected
```

Reads naturally, easy to search, groups well alphabetically. Rules: object first, past-tense verb, Title Case with spaces.

### Option B: `object.action` (snake_case)

```
todo.created
user.invited
search.performed
integration.connected
```

Works in all databases without quoting, easy to parse programmatically. Rules: object first, dot separator, all lowercase with underscores for multi-word.

| Consideration | Object Verb | object.action |
|---|---|---|
| Readability in dashboards | Better | Good |
| Database compatibility | Needs quoting | Native |
| Programmatic parsing | Harder | Easier |

**Pick one. Be consistent. Don't mix.**

### Multi-Word Objects

Keep the same pattern:

**Title Case:** `Advanced Search Performed`, `Bulk Export Generated`, `Setup Wizard Completed`, `User Role Changed`

**Dot notation:** `advanced_search.performed`, `bulk_export.generated`, `setup_wizard.completed`, `user_role.changed`

Do not abbreviate to avoid multi-word names — clarity beats brevity.

### Singular vs Plural Objects

```
Todo Created          -- one todo was created
Todos Cleared         -- all todos were removed at once
Report Exported       -- one report
Reports Bulk Deleted  -- batch operation on many reports
```

### Action Vocabulary

| Action | Meaning |
|--------|---------|
| `created` | New thing made |
| `updated` | Existing thing modified |
| `deleted` | Thing removed |
| `viewed` | Thing displayed to user (use sparingly) |
| `started` | Process began |
| `completed` | Process finished |
| `failed` | Process errored |
| `abandoned` | Process left incomplete (workflows/wizards) |
| `sent` | Message/notification dispatched |
| `received` | Message/notification arrived |
| `connected` | Integration/service linked |
| `disconnected` | Integration/service unlinked |
| `configured` | Settings/setup established |
| `invited` | User invited someone |
| `joined` | User accepted invite |
| `left` | User departed |
| `upgraded` | Plan/tier increased |
| `downgraded` | Plan/tier decreased |
| `generated` | Output produced (reports, exports) |
| `applied` | Filter/template/rule put into effect |
| `performed` | Action executed (search, sync) |

**Avoid `clicked` and `viewed`:** These describe UI mechanics, not user intent. Track meaningful outcomes instead. If you must track navigation, keep it to key pages only.

## When to Create a New Event vs. Use Properties

**Use properties (one event, different property values) for variants of the same action:**

```
report.created  { report_type: 'standard' }
report.created  { report_type: 'custom' }
report.created  { report_type: 'template' }
```

**Use separate events for fundamentally different actions:**

```
report.created
report.shared
report.exported
report.archived
```

**The test:** Can you write a single sentence describing all variants? "A report was created" covers all types — use one event with a property. But "a report was created" and "a report was shared" are different — use separate events.

Why this matters: One event with properties lets you query "all reports created" and break down by type. Separate events per variant explode the event count and make aggregate queries painful. But collapsing genuinely different actions into one event with an `action_type` property obscures what actually happened.

## Property Names

**Format: `snake_case`** — always, regardless of event naming format.

```javascript
{
  report_id: 'rpt_123',
  report_type: 'standard',
  created_by: 'usr_456',
  is_template: false
}
```

### Naming Patterns (Self-Describing Suffixes)

| Pattern | Type | Examples |
|---------|------|----------|
| `*_id` | String (prefixed) | `report_id`, `task_id` |
| `*_type` | Enum string | `report_type: 'standard'` |
| `*_count` | Integer | `recipient_count: 3` |
| `is_*` | Boolean | `is_template: true` |
| `has_*` | Boolean | `has_description: true` |
| `*_at` | ISO 8601 timestamp | `created_at`, `expires_at` |
| `*_source` | Enum string | `signup_source: 'google_oauth'` |
| `*_format` | Enum string | `export_format: 'pdf'` |

**Consistency rule:** If `report_id` appears on two events, it must reference the same entity in the same format. Never reuse a property name with a different meaning.

### Common Properties (Include Consistently)

| Property | Format | Notes |
|----------|--------|-------|
| `user_id` | `usr_xxx` | Always include |
| `account_id` | `acc_xxx` | Always include (B2B) |
| `session_id` | `ses_xxx` | If tracking sessions |
| `timestamp` | ISO 8601 | Usually auto-added by SDK |

### ID Formats

Use prefixed IDs for self-documenting clarity:

| Entity | Prefix | Example |
|--------|--------|---------|
| User | `usr_` | `usr_abc123` |
| Account | `acc_` | `acc_def456` |
| Report | `rpt_` | `rpt_ghi789` |
| Task | `tsk_` | `tsk_jkl012` |
| Team | `tem_` | `tem_mno345` |
| Session | `ses_` | `ses_pqr678` |

## Centralized Event Definitions

**Problem:** Events defined inline wherever they appear lead to typos and phantom duplicates.

```javascript
// File A: 'user performed search'
// File B: 'Search Performed'
// File C: 'SEARCH_EXECUTED'
```

**Solution:** Define all events in one central file. Every tracking call references the definition. This gives you:
- Single audit point for all events
- Typo prevention through reusable definitions
- Easy discovery of what is tracked
- Consistency enforced by structure, not discipline

For larger applications, organize by domain (user events, billing events, etc.) but keep all definitions in a known location.

## User & Account Traits

Traits are stable attributes that persist across events. Unlike event properties, traits build a comprehensive profile over time.

**User Traits (via `identify()`):**

```javascript
identify('usr_123', {
  email: 'jane@example.com',
  name: 'Jane Smith',
  role: 'admin',
  created_at: '2024-01-15T10:30:00Z',
  subscription_level: 'pro',
  preferred_language: 'English',
  last_login: '2024-02-07T10:30:00Z',
  account_id: 'acc_456'
});
```

**Account Traits (via `group()`):**

```javascript
group('acc_456', {
  name: 'Acme Corp',
  plan: 'enterprise',
  industry: 'technology',
  employee_count: 150,
  mrr: 999,
  created_at: '2023-06-01T00:00:00Z',
  number_of_users: 50,
  billing_cycle: 'annual',
  support_level: 'priority'
});
```

## Event Naming Checklist

Before adding a new event:

- [ ] Follows your chosen naming format consistently
- [ ] Uses past tense verb
- [ ] Object comes first, verb comes last
- [ ] Describes the outcome, not the UI mechanism
- [ ] No redundant prefixes (`Event:`, `Track:`, `App.`)
- [ ] No implementation details (`Button1`, `div#search-input`)
- [ ] No PII in the event name
- [ ] Consistent with existing events for the same object
- [ ] Added to the central event definition file
- [ ] Would not be better served by an existing event with a new property value

## Examples by Category

**Lifecycle:** `user.signed_up`, `user.invited`, `user.onboarded`, `user.churned`, `account.created`

**Core Value (Analytics example):** `report.created`, `report.viewed`, `report.exported`, `report.shared`, `dashboard.created`, `dashboard.customized`, `insight.generated`

**Collaboration:** `teammate.invited`, `teammate.joined`, `teammate.removed`, `comment.added`, `mention.created`, `permission.changed`

**Configuration:** `integration.connected`, `integration.disconnected`, `setting.changed`, `webhook.configured`, `api_key.created`

**Billing-Adjacent:** `trial.started`, `trial.extended`, `plan.viewed`, `plan.upgraded`, `plan.downgraded`, `limit.reached`
